evidence.mechanism_source_span: The proposed mechanism incorporates a 143 g lightweight lifting wing and a dual-actuator drive system, with a total structural mass penalty of only 209 g.

mechanism.mechanism: High-performance ground vehicle equipped with a variable-incidence aerodynamic surface that decouples body pitch attitude from local angle of attack (AoA) via a lightweight dual-actuator drive system, ensuring optimal lift-to-drag performance and alleviating detrimental rotor-wing interference.
mechanism.intervention: Implement a dual-actuator drive system with a total structural mass penalty of only 209 g to drive variable-incidence surfaces, reestablishing strong suction peaks on the upper surface at high speeds while maintaining stability.
mechanism.expected_effect: Significant reduction in aerodynamic drag and powertrain energy losses, achieving a maximum normalized power-saving ratio of 42.98% relative to hover and a net 13.22% efficiency improvement over fixed-incidence concepts.
mechanism.falsification_test: The mechanism is falsified if the dual-actuator drive system exceeds the 209 g structural mass penalty or fails to achieve the projected 42.98% power-saving ratio in high-speed testing.

competing_candidates.mechanism: Decoupling fuselage attitude from wing aerodynamics using a variable-incidence lifting surface and dual-actuator drive system.
competing_candidates.intervention: Implement an active, variable-incidence rear wing on the ground vehicle that independently adjusts its angle of attack relative to the chassis pitch to maintain optimal lift-to-drag ratios at extreme velocities.

competing_candidates.mechanism: Decoupling the vehicle's static body attitude from the aerodynamic angle of attack of a passive lifting element allows the element to maintain an optimal lift-to-drag ratio independent of the vehicle's primary pitch orientation, thereby maximizing passive lift and minimizing net aerodynamic drag across varying speeds.
competing_candidates.intervention: Integrate a variable-incidence wing or lifting surface with a dual-actuator drive system that adjusts the angle of attack independently of the chassis pitch, with a total structural mass penalty of 209 g.
competing_candidates.what_would_kill_it: At a vehicle pitch of -20° and a wing AoA of 10°-12°, the device will exhibit a strong suction peak on the upper surface, resulting in a 42.98% reduction in power required compared to a fixed-incidence baseline at 10 m/s.

competing_candidates.intervention: Configure the control strategy to specifically target the alleviation of interference effects by adjusting the wing AoA to 10°-12° when the fuselage pitch is -20°, utilizing high-fidelity CFD-optimized profiles.
competing_candidates.what_would_kill_it: When the vehicle operates at a pitch of -20° and the wing AoA is set to 10°-12%, the passive lift force will increase sufficiently to extend the maximum operational range to 28.1 km, showing high consistency between numerical predictions and experimental data.

competing_candidates.mechanism: Decoupling fuselage attitude from wing aerodynamics enables the vehicle to maintain optimal lift-to-drag performance across varying flight speeds, providing a robust and highly efficient solution for extending endurance in energy-constrained environments by allowing the vehicle to adapt its aerodynamic profile independently of its stability attitude.
competing_candidates.intervention: Implement a decoupling control strategy that allows the lifting wing to adjust its incidence to optimize efficiency without constraining the main vehicle's pitch attitude, utilizing a lightweight 143 g wing structure.
competing_candidates.what_would_kill_it: Systematic tests at 10 m/s will demonstrate a 42.98% power-saving ratio relative to hover when the decoupling control strategy is active, proving the design provides a net 13.22% efficiency improvement over fixed-incidence concepts.

evidence.mechanism_source_span: The aerodynamic efficiency of conventional lifting-wing quadrotors is severely constrained by the rigid coupling between fuselage pitch attitude and wing angle of attack (AoA), which prevents the vehicle from maintaining optimal lift-to-drag performance across varying flight speeds.

mechanism.mechanism: Decoupling the vehicle's static body attitude from the aerodynamic angle of attack of a passive lifting element allows the element to maintain an optimal lift-to-drag ratio independent of the vehicle's primary pitch orientation, thereby maximizing passive lift and minimizing net aerodynamic drag across varying speeds.
mechanism.intervention: Integrate a variable-incidence wing or lifting surface with a dual-actuator drive system that adjusts the angle of attack independently of the chassis pitch, with a total structural mass penalty of 209 g.
mechanism.expected_effect: Reduction in normalized power-saving ratio at 10 m/s relative to hover, with a net 13.22% efficiency improvement over fixed-incidence concepts after accounting for weight penalties.
mechanism.falsification_test: At a vehicle pitch of -20° and a wing AoA of 10°-12°, the device will exhibit a strong suction peak on the upper surface, resulting in a 42.98% reduction in power required compared to a fixed-incidence baseline at 10 m/s.
